samples.answer: Rust ensures memory safety without garbage collection through ownership and borrowing. Every value has a single owner, and when the owner goes out of scope, the value is dropped. You can borrow references to data instead of transferring ownership. Rust enforces strict rules: you can have either one mutable reference or any number of immutable references at a time, but never both. This prevents data races and dangling pointers at compile time. By managing memory through these compile-time checks, Rust eliminates common bugs like use-after-free errors while maintaining high performance and zero-cost abstractions.
